name: ConvertNow Analytics: Website Stats, Visitor Counter and AI Traffic
author: Prateek Zare

sections.description:
Simple, private and free WordPress analytics that count real people, not bots.

Most stats plugins count everything that loads a page. Bots, crawlers, uptime monitors and AI scrapers all end up in your visitor numbers. Your traffic can look twice as big as it really is.

ConvertNow Analytics counts a visit only when a real person sees the page. Every bot it leaves out is listed by name, so you can check the numbers yourself.

No cookies. No Google account. No paid plan. Your data stays in your own WordPress database.

Want to try it first? Press Live Preview above to open a full demo with 90 days of sample traffic.

Why people switch to ConvertNow

  • Real visitors only. Bots, crawlers, fake Googlebots and rendering farms are filtered out and shown separately.
  • See your AI traffic. Find out how many readers ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini, Claude and Copilot send you.
  • Privacy friendly. No cookies and no stored IP addresses. Many sites run it without a cookie banner.
  • Easy to read. Clear reports in plain English, in light or dark mode.
  • Fast. A tiny tracker of about 6 KB that loads from your own site.
  • 100% free. No pro version, no license key and nothing locked.

Get started in a minute

  1. Go to Plugins, Add New and search for ConvertNow Analytics.
  2. Click Install Now, then Activate.
  3. Open ConvertNow in the admin menu.

That’s it. There is no code to paste and no account to create. Tracking starts right away, and caching plugins, CDNs and Cloudflare are handled for you.

Website stats at a glance

  • Visitors, visits, page views, bounce rate and time on page
  • Real time visitors, plus today’s visitors in the admin bar
  • Compare with the period before, the same dates last year or any range you pick
  • Countries on a world map, languages, devices, browsers and screen sizes
  • A dashboard widget on your WordPress home screen

Know which posts people read

  • Page views for every post and page, with a sortable Views column in your post list
  • Each post’s numbers right inside the block editor
  • Read depth, time on page and scroll depth for every page
  • Top pages, landing pages, exit pages, authors, categories and tags
  • Launch curve: see how a new post is doing against your usual post
  • A Popular Posts block in four styles (numbered, list, cards and image grid) and an optional post views counter for readers

See where your traffic comes from

  • Search engines, social networks, referrers and UTM campaign tracking
  • Channels close to Google Analytics, such as organic search, paid, social and email
  • AI traffic analytics: visits from ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini, Claude, Copilot, DeepSeek and more
  • AI crawler tracking: see GPTBot, ClaudeBot, PerplexityBot and other AI bots by name, and the pages they read

Track goals, forms and sales

  • Goals and conversion tracking for any page or form
  • Funnels, user journeys, retention, cohorts and segments
  • Contact form tracking for Contact Form 7, WPForms, Gravity Forms, Fluent Forms, Formidable, Ninja Forms and Elementor
  • Outbound link, file download, email and phone click tracking
  • Affiliate link tracking for Amazon, ShareASale, Awin, CJ, Impact and more
  • WooCommerce and Easy Digital Downloads revenue by source, campaign and page
  • Site search terms and 404 pages

Page speed and engagement

  • Core Web Vitals (LCP, INP and CLS) from your real visitors, by page and device
  • How far down each page people scroll, and where most of them stop
  • Which pages hold attention, and how people move from page to page

Reports and alerts by email

  • A daily, weekly or monthly summary email with a short AI brief
  • Each person picks the report that fits their job: owner, editor, marketer, shop or technical
  • Alerts when traffic drops or spikes, with the likely cause and what to do
  • Your own alert rules, by email, Slack or Discord

Bot filtering you can trust

A visit only counts when a real browser shows the page on screen and a person is there to see it. Crawlers, headless browsers, rendering farms, uptime monitors and cloud servers are refused. Requests that pretend to be Googlebot or another known crawler are caught too. You can see all of it under Filtered Traffic, by name and by reason.

A privacy friendly Google Analytics alternative

Visitors are counted with an anonymous code that changes every day. No cookies are set and no IP addresses are stored. Nothing about your visitors is ever sent to another company. It is built to be GDPR and CCPA friendly, and many sites use it without a cookie banner for analytics. Settings gives you a ready to paste paragraph for your privacy policy.

Switch without losing your history

Moving from another tool? Import your past traffic from Google Analytics 4, Independent Analytics, Burst Statistics, Koko Analytics, WP Statistics, Matomo, Plausible or any CSV export. Preview first and undo any time.

Free for agencies too

Put your own logo and colours on the dashboard and emails. Give clients a read only login, send them a branded monthly report, and copy your setup to the next client site in one step.

Who it’s for

  • Bloggers and publishers who want to know what people actually read
  • Small businesses that want to see where customers come from
  • Online stores that want revenue by traffic source
  • Affiliate sites that want to see which links earn clicks
  • Agencies that manage many client sites

50+ reports in all, with filters, presets and CSV export.

Links: Documentation · Support forum · contact@convertnow.tools

External services

Tracking, reporting, goals, funnels, journeys, retention, segments, cohorts, insights, alerts, country lookups and exports all run on your own server against your own database. There is no activation call, no licence check and no key. Nothing about your visitors ever leaves your site under any setting. The plugin makes the background requests below, and each one can be switched off.

Apple iCloud Private Relay exit list (on by default)

Once a week the plugin downloads https://mask-api.icloud.com/egress-ip-ranges.csv, the list Apple publishes of the addresses Private Relay traffic leaves from. It is used only so that Safari readers using Private Relay are not refused as data centre traffic. The request sends nothing but your server’s own address, the way any download does. Switch it off in Settings, Tracking, Data centre addresses. Apple’s terms: apple.com/legal/internet-services/terms/site.html. Apple’s privacy policy: apple.com/legal/privacy.

Site icons (on by default)

Icons for the major search engines, social networks and AI assistants ship inside the plugin and need no request at all. For any other referring site, the plugin fetches its icon in the background from the site’s own address (its home page and /favicon.ico, then the parent domain for a subdomain). When a site refuses requests from servers, the icon is fetched from DuckDuckGo’s public icon service at https://icons.duckduckgo.com/ip3/, which is told the site’s host name and nothing else. Fetched icons are stored under uploads and served from your own site; opening the dashboard requests nothing from anybody else. Switch fetching off in Settings, Display, Site icons (bundled icons still show), or keep it and stop only the DuckDuckGo fallback with the cnwa_icon_fallback_service filter. DuckDuckGo’s terms: duckduckgo.com/terms. DuckDuckGo’s privacy policy: duckduckgo.com/privacy.

Alert webhook (off by default)

If you enter a webhook address under Settings, Alerts, each alert is posted to that address, and only to that address. The request carries the alert’s title and sentence, your site’s address and a link to the dashboard. Where it goes is the service you chose, under that service’s own terms.

Report a bug (only when you press Send)

Settings has a Report a bug card. When an administrator presses Send report, your site’s own mail sends one email to contact@convertnow.tools, the author’s support address, with the description and reply address you typed and, unless you untick it, a diagnostic report. The report is shown in full on that screen before you send it: your site address, WordPress, PHP and database versions, active plugins and theme, this plugin’s settings with every address and email field left out, Tracking health, daily totals, table sizes and the plugin’s own lines from the debug log, with any address in them masked. It never contains visitor IP addresses, visitor hashes, page paths or anything else about your visitors. Nothing is sent at any other time. The same report can be downloaded as a text file instead.

Anonymous usage reporting (off by default)

If, and only if, you switch this on, the plugin sends one report a month, and one after each plugin update, to convertnow.tools, the author’s site, at https://convertnow.tools/wp-json/cnwa-hub/v1/report. It exists so the author can see which versions are in use and how the plugin is actually being used, and it is used for nothing else.

It is off on every install. You are asked once, on the plugin’s own screen and only after the plugin has a week of your own data, with the exact payload from your site shown to you before you decide. Declining is remembered permanently. If you never answer, nothing is ever sent. You can switch it on or off at any time in Settings, Data retention, Anonymous usage report. Switching it off removes the scheduled event immediately and sends one last request to the same address, carrying only your site address, the install date and the plugin version, which asks convertnow.tools to delete every report your site sent. Nothing is sent after that.

This is the complete payload, and there is nothing else in it:

  • Your site address and site name
  • The date this plugin was first activated on your site
  • Your total pageviews and total visitors for the last 30 days, as two numbers
  • The ConvertNow, WordPress and PHP versions, and your site locale

It contains nothing about your visitors: no page paths, no referrers, no IP addresses, no visitor hashes, no user accounts, no email addresses, no post or page titles. The request is sent once every 30 days and once after each update, and a failure is silent.

Terms of service: convertnow.tools/terms. Privacy policy: convertnow.tools/privacy.

Requests to your own site

The daily health check loads your own home page and posts a test beacon to your own collector, both at your own address. Nothing leaves your server.

The country lookup tables and the address lists that Google, Bing, Apple, DuckDuckGo, OpenAI and Perplexity publish for their crawlers ship inside the plugin and are read from disk. There is nothing to download and nothing to import.Links

  • Plugin home page: convertnow.tools/convertnow-analytics
  • Support by email: contact@convertnow.tools or prateekzare@gmail.com
  • Support forum: wordpress.org/support/plugin/convertnow-analytics
  • Leave a review: wordpress.org/support/plugin/convertnow-analytics/reviews

Bundled data

IP Geolocation by DB-IP, used under CC BY 4.0.

Data centre detection reads two plain text tables built from the X4BNet datacenter lists, MIT licensed, plus a short supplement of documented cloud supernets: assets/data/dc-ipv4.csv and assets/data/dc-ipv6.csv, in the same boundary format as the country tables. The build script is tools/build-dc-tables.py in the development sources.

Brand icons in assets/icons/ come from SVG Logos and Simple Icons (CC0), Lobe Icons (MIT) and Font Awesome Free (CC BY 4.0). assets/icons/CREDITS.txt lists which is which. Every trademark belongs to its owner; the icons are used only to identify the site a visit came from.

Crawler checks read includes/crawler-ranges.php, built from the address lists Google, Bing, Apple, DuckDuckGo, OpenAI and Perplexity publish for their own crawlers.

Country lookups read two plain text tables built from the DB-IP IP to Country Lite database: assets/data/geo-ipv4.csv and assets/data/geo-ipv6.csv. Every line is one boundary, written as an uppercase hex address prefix and an ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code, so both files can be opened and read in any text editor. The world map outlines are plain JSON path data at assets/data/world.json. Nothing in the plugin is compiled, minified or obfuscated.
sections.installation:
1. Go to Plugins, Add New and search for ConvertNow Analytics.
  2. Click Install Now, then Activate.
  3. Open ConvertNow in the admin menu.

No key, no account and no setup. Counting starts right away.

Your own visits are not counted while you are logged in as an administrator or editor, so the numbers start at zero until real visitors arrive. To look around first, switch on Test mode at the top of the Stats screen. It fills every report with sample data from a made up coffee shop. Switch back to Live whenever you like. Real visits keep counting the whole time.
sections.faq:
Is it a good Google Analytics alternative?

Yes, for most WordPress sites. It shows the reports people open Google Analytics for: visitors, pages, sources, campaigns, countries, devices, goals and sales. Everything is inside WordPress, with no cookies and no Google account.

How is it different from Jetpack Stats, Site Kit or MonsterInsights?

Site Kit and MonsterInsights show Google Analytics data, so Google still tracks your visitors and you usually need a cookie banner. Jetpack Stats sends each visit to WordPress.com. ConvertNow counts on your own server, removes bots before they reach your numbers, and is free with every feature included.

Is it GDPR compliant? Do I need a cookie banner?

It sets no cookies, stores nothing on the visitor’s device and never keeps raw IP addresses. All data stays on your server. That is why many sites use it without a cookie banner for analytics. Rules differ by country, so check with your own legal advisor.

Can it track traffic from ChatGPT and other AI tools?

Yes. Visits from ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini, Claude, Copilot, DeepSeek and other assistants get their own AI channel, with the pages each one sends people to. AI crawlers like GPTBot and ClaudeBot are shown separately, because a crawler is not a reader.

Why are my numbers lower than Google Analytics or Jetpack?

Usually because ConvertNow removes what other tools count. Bots and AI crawlers are filtered out, a page has to be seen by a real person, and your own logged in team is skipped. It also starts counting on the day you install it. Filtered Traffic shows exactly what was left out.

Will it slow down my site?

No. The tracker is about 6 KB, loads from your own site and makes no outside requests. Reports read from daily summaries, so the dashboard stays fast on large and busy sites.

Does it work with caching plugins, CDNs and Cloudflare?

Yes. Cached pages still report their visits, and popular speed plugins are told to leave the tracker alone. Because the tracker loads from your own site, most ad blockers do not stop it. Tracking health checks your live pages and tells you if anything is in the way.

Does it work with WooCommerce?

Yes. WooCommerce and Easy Digital Downloads orders are linked to the visit that made them. You see revenue by source, campaign, landing page and author, and the totals match your shop.

Can I import my old stats?

Yes. Go to ConvertNow, Import. You can bring history from Google Analytics 4, Independent Analytics, Burst Statistics, Koko Analytics, WP Statistics, Matomo, Plausible or any CSV file. Only days before ConvertNow started counting are filled, and you can undo it.

Can I see page views for each post?

Yes. Every post and page shows its views, visitors, time on page and read depth. Your post list gets a sortable Views column, and the block editor shows each post’s numbers. You can also show a view count or a Popular Posts list to your readers.

Can I use it on client sites?

Yes, for free. Agency mode adds your name, logo and colours, gives clients a read only login and sends them a branded report by email.

Where is my data stored?

In your own WordPress database. Uninstalling keeps your data by default, so a reinstall picks up where you left off. Switch on full removal in Settings to delete everything.
sections.changelog:
1.9.0

New

  • Compare any two date ranges: the period before, the same dates last year or a range you pick.
  • Core Web Vitals from your real visitors: LCP, INP and CLS by page and device.
  • Scroll Reach: how far down each page people read, and where most of them stop.
  • Launch Curve: how each new post starts against your usual post.
  • Popular Posts block with numbered, list, card and image grid layouts, images, excerpts, dates, authors, view counts, a category filter and your theme’s colours, plus the [cnwa_popular] shortcode and an optional view count on posts with [cnwa_views].
  • Ready to paste text for your privacy or cookie policy in Settings, written from your own settings, also added to the WordPress Privacy Policy Guide.
  • The version and a What’s new link in the footer of the Stats screen, and beside the version in Settings and Documentation, to read this version’s notes again.
  • A sortable Views column in Posts and Pages, and a 30 day chart in the block editor.
  • Form goals for Contact Form 7, WPForms, Gravity Forms, Fluent Forms, Formidable, Ninja Forms and Elementor.
  • Affiliate Links: outbound clicks grouped by program, including Amazon, ShareASale, Awin, CJ and Impact, plus your own /go/ links.
  • Categories and Tags report.
  • Summary emails and alerts for each person, with a choice of report and an AI brief.
  • Smarter alerts that name the likely cause, plus alerts for falling conversions, stopped orders, slow pages and new referrers, and alerts you write yourself.
  • A dashboard widget with a range and four cards you pick.

Better counting

  • Rendering farms that scroll pages by script are filtered and listed under their own kind, Rendering farm.
  • One browser tab opening more than 20 pages in an hour without any mouse, tap or key is filtered.
  • Your own team stays out of the numbers on cached pages too.
  • Fake Googlebots and other crawlers using a borrowed name are caught and listed as fakes.
  • AI and search crawlers are sorted more accurately, and unknown crawlers show their own name.
  • AI referrals from the ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Perplexity, Copilot, DeepSeek, Grok, Meta AI, Mistral, Doubao and Kimi apps are credited to the right assistant.

Faster

  • The tracker is about 6 KB compressed.
  • Scroll Reach stays quick on sites with millions of views.

1.8.4

Steadier numbers: untouched home page visits from one network are capped, Tracking health says when a consent banner holds back Jetpack Stats or Google Analytics, and Documentation explains how ConvertNow compares with other tools.

1.8.3

Rendering farms are filtered: a view with no referrer, nothing touched and a browser clock hours away from its country, or from a near square desktop screen no monitor is sold in, is filed under Filtered Traffic as headless. Readers abroad or on a VPN who scroll, tap or arrive from a link are counted. What’s new also lists the counting changes of skipped releases, and the early translation notice beside WP Statistics is gone.

1.8.2

ChatGPT, Qwen, Kimi and other AI readers are credited as AI traffic, a utm_source that names a site is credited to that site, channels are one fixed list close to Google Analytics, click ids count as paid clicks, ad networks count as display, newer AI crawlers are named, and site icons are redrawn as fresh PNG files so hosting malware scanners have nothing to flag.

1.8.1

Each post’s views where you work on it: in the admin bar while you edit or view it, in a ConvertNow panel in the block editor, in a Views column in your post lists, and behind an Analytics link on every row. The ConvertNow logo in the admin bar.

1.8.0

Import your history from Independent Analytics, Burst, Koko, WP Statistics, Matomo, Plausible, Google Analytics or any export, with a preview and undo. Presets, default filters and multi value filters on the Stats screen. Agency settings profiles, client invites, client reports and a settings lock, and Report a bug in Settings.

1.7.3

Each reader recognised once: unknown proxies and CDNs are spotted and trusted with one click, IPv6 readers stay one visitor, infinite scroll and the Back button no longer count a page twice, gateway errors are retried, and busy sites load much faster.

1.7.2

Small trend lines in every headline tile, and screen notes behind an i button beside the title.

1.7.1

Plain language alert emails that say what happened, whether anything is wrong and what to do, the same clear wording for filtered bots everywhere, and the 1.7.0 What’s new window for sites updating from 1.6.x.

1.7.0

Agency mode with branding, client logins and settings export, colour palettes, test mode, share cards, an admin bar counter and badge, full width screens and an accessibility pass. The tracker loads from your own site, works with the common optimisers and reads Cloudflare directly, plus a database size card and refreshed country and data centre lists.

1.6.6

Counting fixes: same page links and the Back button are handled correctly, no pageview is dropped for arriving too soon, two tabs are one visit, each referrer site has one name, channels are stricter and comparisons are exact. AI insights catch source drops and steady AI growth. Adds a What’s new window after updates.

1.6.5

AI insights rebuilt as tested models: unusual days with causes, change points, a backtested forecast, page trends and AI citation gaps.

1.6.4

Tracking health readable in dark mode, and five new charts on the Calendar screen.

1.6.3

Summary emails every day, week, two weeks or month, fuller documentation, and SQLite support for the Live Preview.

1.6.2

Fixes missing names in the Top countries list.

1.6.1

Customisable report screens, fairer channel credit for later pages, revenue that matches your shop, and new Explore, Engagement, Page Flow, AI and Calendar screens.

1.6.0

Rebuilds no longer delete older history. Adds a first run checklist, a customisable Stats screen and the llms.txt report.

1.5.0 and 1.5.1

Tracking health checks, alerts by email or webhook, site icons, iCloud Private Relay support and about a hundred bundled site icons.

1.4.0 and 1.4.1

Counts people only: cloud servers, headless browsers and pages nobody touched are refused. Filtered Traffic rebuilt.

1.3.0 to 1.3.2

Revenue reporting for WooCommerce and Easy Digital Downloads, correct counting behind caches and CDNs, and a pageview that has to prove a person was there.

1.0.0 to 1.2.3

First release with editorial reports, then AI Visibility, insights, an optional usage report and a series of accuracy fixes.

Switching it off removes the scheduled event immediately and sends one last request to the same address, carrying only your site address, the install date and the plugin version, which asks convertnow.tools to delete every report your site sent. Nothing is sent after that.

This is the complete payload, and there is nothing else in it:

  • Your site address and site name
  • The date this plugin was first activated on your site
  • Your total pageviews and total visitors for the last 30 days, as two numbers
  • The ConvertNow, WordPress and PHP versions, and your site locale

It contains nothing about your visitors: no page paths, no referrers, no IP addresses, no visitor hashes, no user accounts, no email addresses, no post or page titles. The request is sent once every 30 days and once after each update, and a failure is silent.

Requests to your own site

The daily health check loads your own home page and posts a test beacon to your own collector, both at your own address. Nothing leaves your server.

The country lookup tables and the address lists that Google, Bing, Apple, DuckDuckGo, OpenAI and Perplexity publish for their crawlers ship inside the plugin and are read from disk. There is nothing to download and nothing to import.Links

Bundled data

IP Geolocation by DB-IP, used under CC BY 4.0.

Data centre detection reads two plain text tables built from the X4BNet datacenter lists, MIT licensed, plus a short supplement of documented cloud supernets: assets/data/dc-ipv4.csv and assets/data/dc-ipv6.csv, in the same boundary format as the country tables. The build script is tools/build-dc-tables.py in the development sources.

Brand icons in assets/icons/ come from SVG Logos and Simple Icons (CC0), Lobe Icons (MIT) and Font Awesome Free (CC BY 4.0). assets/icons/CREDITS.txt lists which is which. Every trademark belongs to its owner; the icons are used only to identify the site a visit came from.

Crawler checks read includes/crawler-ranges.php, built from the address lists Google, Bing, Apple, DuckDuckGo, OpenAI and Perplexity publish for their own crawlers.

Country lookups read two plain text tables built from the DB-IP IP to Country Lite database: assets/data/geo-ipv4.csv and assets/data/geo-ipv6.csv. Every line is one boundary, written as an uppercase hex address prefix and an ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code, so both files can be opened and read in any text editor. The world map outlines are plain JSON path data at assets/data/world.json. Nothing in the plugin is compiled, minified or obfuscated.
